result.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
result.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends. We compare a modular pipeline, with separate step identification, temporal localization, and execution verification, to a joint model that predicts all outputs in a single step. To support supervised learning from mistakes, we repartition EgoPER to include erroneous videos in all splits. The approaches achieve similar step-segmentation F1@0.5 (93.6% and 92.1%), while the joint model achieves higher binary mistake-detection F1@0.5 (84.1% vs. 80.7%), with its largest gain on slips (56.4% vs. 37.5%). Component-level analysis suggests that error propagation between stages contributes to the modular approach's lower detection score. On test videos containing mistakes, both designs outperform released AEM and ESTANet checkpoints under our evaluation protocol.

AI.brief_summary: 研究第一视角程序性视频中的在线、指令条件化错误检测：仅用已观测视频、任务指令与历史预测，实时识别并定位动作尝试并判定其为正确、修改、失误、纠正或多余，并比较模块化流水线与单步联合模型两种设计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「联合预测 vs 分阶段流水线」的对照与阶段间误差传播分析，可能为 LVR 中多阶段 latent 状态的贡献分配、监督放置与流水线式推理设计提供核查线索，但论文本身不涉及 VLM 内部表示或 latent 推理。
